The Puchi family opened the first Bajamar on Las Vegas Blvd in 2017 to bring a Baja California surf shack to town. Locals took to it. This is the same food and the same loud, friendly room, now on the southwest side.

Order for pickup

Created in Baja. Born in Vegas.

More than a restaurant. A place where first-time guests leave feeling like regulars.

The Puchi family opened the first Bajamar Seafood & Tacos on Las Vegas Blvd in 2017, with one idea: a Baja California surf shack, in Vegas. The locals took to it and, in Alberto Puchi's words, blessed it with support through the pandemic and beyond.

Since then Bajamar has grown across the valley. The Rainbow Blvd location brings the same fresh seafood, the same salsas made in house, and the same room where the game is on and the aguachile hits, to the southwest side.

What to expect

Order at the counter

Walk up, order, grab a table. Open kitchen, so you can watch it come together.

Seafood first

Tacos, ceviche tostadas, aguachile, seafood cocktails. Simple Baja flavors, fish is the star.

Game on, salsa hot

TVs, a surfboard on the wall, homemade habanero on the table. Family and game-day friendly.

The Rainbow room

A casual Baja surf shack in the Rainbow Sunset plaza. Reclaimed-wood tables, black metal chairs, string lights, a painted octopus mural, a surfboard on the wall, and TVs with the game on. Big storefront windows onto the lot. Order at the counter and watch the open kitchen work.

  • ParkingFree surface lot, shared with the plaza
  • Getting hereOff S Rainbow Blvd near the 215 Beltway, southwest Las Vegas
  • Good forWalk-ins, families, game day, quick lunch
